t: #3662 Filter Characters by Frequency — Counting Filter
o: Count each character's frequency in s, then rebuild the string keeping only characters whose total count is below k, preserving order. With |s| ≤ 100 any counting method works; the interesting choice is hash map versus a fixed 26-slot array.
k: One pass to count, one pass to filter — frequencies are global, not positional.
Order preservation is automatic when filtering in a single left-to-right scan.

a.i: Use a Counter/dictionary for frequencies, then a generator over s keeps characters with count < k.
s: Join the characters of s whose count < k.

a.i: Since the alphabet is fixed lowercase letters, a 26-element array avoids hashing overhead entirely — marginally faster and language-idiomatic in C++/Java.
s: Filter in pass two using the array.

w: Both are fine; mention the array version shows alphabet awareness. Pitfalls: comparing against ≤ k instead of < k, and accidentally deduplicating (every occurrence below threshold must be kept). Follow-up: keep characters occurring at least k times, or apply per-window frequencies.
